title: POC weekly stability audit and guardrail tuning with Lakestone Logistics
summary: Weekly POC sync focused on recent regression spike in entity extraction and guardrail false positives. Team reviewed scorecard changes after prompt set update, agreed to run expanded evals and a latency/throughput benchmark, and to push a short-term prompt rollback for the highest-severity cases. Redwood to share updated security checklist and a short repro harness for the customer to run in their staging env.
topics: guardrail false positives vs false negatives
next_steps: Redwood: share security checklist + SOC2 summary (Maya) by 2026-12-04
Customer: run Redwood repro harness in staging and return eval logs by 2026-12-09
Redwood SE: submit rollback patch for prompt-set alpha and deploy to pilot variant by 2026-12-06
action_items: Maya Chen: send SOC2 + encryption/KMS notes and link to secure bucket (due: 2026-12-04)
Ethan Brooks: prepare rollback prompt patch and short test harness (due: 2026-12-06)
Samir Patel: collect 1k additional failure examples and push to shared eval sheet (due: 2026-12-07)
Dylan Mercer: provision staging instance and run Redwood repro harness (due: 2026-12-09)
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-02 15:00 PST
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Lina (Redwood CSM), Priya (Lakestone Head of AI), Dylan (Eng Mgr), Samir (Data Scientist), Ava (Product)

Auto-generated summary: brief, may be incomplete. See action items.

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call?
[00:03] Priya: Hi, Priya here — running a bit late this morning but all good.
[00:06] Dylan: Dylan here.
[00:07] Samir: Samir — good afternoon.
[00:09] Ethan: Ethan, Redwood SE.
[00:11] Maya: Great. Agenda — quick review of last week's scorecard, dig into the regression spike on entity extraction, decide on rollback vs tweak, and plan benchmarks.
[00:20] Priya: Before we get too deep, the spike hit production last night; our ops flagged a 4% drop in precision for consignment ID extraction and about a 2% increase in guardrail blocks for safe content. It's causing some manual triage.
[00:33] Maya: Understood. Can you point to a couple of representative examples in the sheet you shared?
[00:38] Priya: Sure — row 24, 73, 101 — mostly short manifests where the model clipped IDs as dates or combined two tokens. Also we saw some cases where the guardrail flagged benign phrases, e.g., "hazard?" being over-eager.
[00:54] Ethan: Right, we ran the prompt-set alpha last Tuesday which added a short negative-prompt path to reduce hallucinations; initial sims looked good but there was a subtle tokenization change because of the new prefix we inserted. That can push some entity boundaries.
[01:12] Samir: So the timing matches. We rolled alpha at 01:00 UTC yesterday to pilot and then saw the uptick.
[01:18] Maya: Good correlation. Two parallel tracks then: rollback alpha immediately for the pilot to recover precision, and run an A/B with a tuned negative-prompt that preserves safe-guardrail sensitivity. Thoughts?
[01:30] Dylan: We prefer rollback if it buys immediate recovery. Our ops queue is against manual review and it's piling up.
[01:36] Priya: Agreed. If rollback is fast and low risk we want that first. Then we can iterate on the prompt tuning offline.
[01:41] Ethan: We can push a rollback to the pilot variant in about 3–4 hours from now; it's a lightweight config change. However, we should also capture the failing inputs and run them through a local sim so we don't lose signal.
[01:53] Maya: OK, Ethan to prepare rollback. Samir you'll collect the failure set and we'll re-run.
[01:58] Samir: Yep, I'll export the 1k samples flagged since midnight. There may be some duplicates and some transcribe noise but should be fine.
[02:07] Ava: Quick question on guardrails: are these implemented at the model level or as a post-filter? Last week we had an odd block that looked like it was triggered earlier in the pipeline.
[02:16] Ethan: It's a mix. We have both a model-level instruction and a downstream classification filter. The classifier uses a separate small model that's been quantized and runs in the host path. Occasionally the classifier is sensitive to phrasing changes from the prompt insertion.
[02:32] Priya: That explains the false positives. The blocking classifier flagged "hazard" in a shipment note even though context clarified it's not a safety event.
[02:40] Maya: For mitigation, we can lower classifier thresholds for non-critical routes and add a context-aware exception for manifest-type docs. But that requires a small engineering change.
[02:49] Dylan: Timeline?
[02:51] Ethan: Threshold change is quick (config tweak), context exception needs a small regex/metadata hook — estimate 2–3 days.
[03:00] Priya: Do the quick fixes first. We still need the rollback.
[03:05] Maya: OK. Switching to scorecard — Samir, can you talk to the numbers and any regressions we've seen by label?
[03:12] Samir: Sure. In the last 48h precision for consignment IDs dropped from 96.4% to 92.1% on the pilot cohort. Recall is mostly unchanged, weirdly. For guardrail false positives, we saw an increase from 1.2% to 3.3% on certain document types. The confusion matrix shows a shift where short token sequences are misclassified.
[03:36] Ethan: That supports the tokenization insertion hypothesis. The new prefix leads to concatenation across boundary tokens for some models, especially with the 4-bit quantized variant we were testing.
[03:47] Priya: Is quantization in our pilot different from prod?
[03:50] Ethan: We run a 4-bit quantized variant in the pilot to reduce cost; prod runs 8-bit in our current setup. Quantization can amplify subtle token boundary issues.
[04:00] Maya: Good catch. So next experiments: (1) rollback prompt set on pilot to recover precision, (2) run the failing 1k through both quantized and non-quantized variants to see sensitivity, (3) tune classifier threshold for manifest route.
[04:18] Dylan: For the broader eval, can Redwood provide a small harness? We prefer a reproducible script rather than ad-hoc calls.
[04:25] Ethan: Yes, I'll attach a lightweight repro harness that runs a batch of examples and outputs tokenization diffs, top-k logits, and the classifier decisions. It's a short Python script that hits the pilot endpoint. We'll provide instructions to run it in staging.
[04:40] Priya: Please include a short doc on how to pin model versions and the rollback path so our SREs can do it without raising a ticket.
[04:47] Lina: We'll include runbook steps and a link to the rollback UI.
[04:52] Maya: On security asks — Priya you emailed a list yesterday — SOC2, SSO, KMS questions. Lina and I will compile the summary and share the secure link.
[05:01] Priya: Great. We also have a compliance review next week that will want an audit trail for any prompt changes.
[05:07] Maya: We'll include change history and timestamps in the runbook export.
[05:11] Samir: A couple of quick technical questions: are we caching prefix tokens or doing dynamic KV cache sharing across requests? We want to understand potential cache leakage between manifests.
[05:21] Ethan: There's no cross-customer KV sharing. We do an intra-request prefix cache per connection; for our pilot variant we set short-lived caches to optimize latency. If manifest headers are included in the prefix it can affect subsequent responses within that connection, but that shouldn't cross file boundaries in your workload.
[05:39] Samir: OK, good. Any plan to run the latency/throughput benchmark against both hosted and dedicated variants? We'll need to know trade-offs for commit decisions.
[05:48] Maya: We proposed a joint benchmark next week — we'll run the hosted pilot path and a dedicated-like config that simulates reserved GPUs. Expect different tail latency and throughput. We'll include token-cost estimates.
[06:02] Dylan: Also can you show us a cost delta if we move from 4-bit quantized pilot to 8-bit in prod? Need to check unit economics.
[06:09] Maya: We'll include a rough delta based on tokens/sec and memory. Ethan can provide model profile numbers.
[06:15] Ethan: I have a profiling sheet; I'll send numbers and the assumptions behind the quantization tradeoffs.
[06:22] Priya: Any competitors or other vendors we should watch? Our procurement asked if Anthropic or OpenAI would handle this differently.
[06:29] Maya: We discussed near-term trade-offs vs Anthropic and OpenAI last quarter. The main difference is in control of tokens and routing — Redwood gives you more guardrail and routing control for hybrid deployments. But we'll provide a comparative note.
[06:41] Samir: One more note — some examples show transcription errors from our upstream OCR; that inflates false positives. We should filter OCR noise before feeding to the eval.
[06:50] Dylan: Good point. We'll include a column for OCR confidence in the export.
[06:54] Maya: OK to summarize next steps: Ethan to prepare rollback + repro harness; Maya/Lina to share security and runbook docs; Samir/Dylan to produce failure set and run the harness. Schedule latency benchmark for 12/08, 60 minutes.
[07:12] Priya: Sounds good. Thanks, all.
[07:15] Maya: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up in the notes and I'll send calendar invite for the benchmark.

End transcript.
